svg.title: The three CARS skills, in AAMC's own words
svg.desc: Three stacked bands, one per AAMC skill, each giving the official sub-skills, the question stems that signal it, and what to do. Skill 1, Foundations of Comprehension, 30 percent: AAMC's sub-skills are understanding the basic components of the text, and inferring meaning or intent from immediate sentence context; stems include the central thesis is, the author's primary purpose is, according to the passage, and as used in paragraph 3 the word most nearly means; the operation is to go back to the text and read what it actually says. Skill 2, Reasoning Within the Text, 30 percent: AAMC's sub-skills are integrating distant components of the text to infer an author's message, intent, purpose, belief, position, bias or assumptions, and recognizing and evaluating arguments and their structural elements, meaning claims, evidence, support and relations; stems include it can be inferred that, the author implies, the author mentions X primarily in order to, and the function of the third paragraph is; the operation is to analyse how the argument is built and infer only what it commits the author to. Skill 3, Reasoning Beyond the Text, 40 percent: AAMC's sub-skills are applying or extrapolating ideas from the passage to new contexts, and assessing the impact of incorporating new factors, information or conditions on ideas from the passage; stems include the author would most likely respond to X by, which situation is most analogous, and which of the following, if true, would most strengthen or weaken; the operation is to use the passage as a lens on new information. A footer notes that errors cascade upward, since misreading the thesis costs you the reasoning questions too, and that the answer is decided by the passage, never by what you already know.
svg.text: The three CARS skills, in AAMC's own words
Foundations 30% · Reasoning Within 30% · Reasoning Beyond 40% — so ~70% is more than comprehension.
Foundations of Comprehension
AAMC skill 1 · 30% of questions
AAMC's two sub-skills
· Understanding the basic components of the text
· Inferring meaning or intent from immediate
sentence context
"The central thesis is…" · "According to the passage…" ·
"As used in ¶3, X most nearly means…"
Go back to the text. Read what it actually says.
Reasoning Within the Text
AAMC skill 2 · 30% of questions
AAMC's two sub-skills
· Integrating distant components of the text to
infer an author's message, intent, purpose, belief,
position, bias, assumptions
· Recognizing and evaluating arguments and their
structural elements (claims, evidence, support,
relations)
"It can be inferred…" · "The author implies…" · "X is
mentioned primarily in order to…"
Analyse how the argument is built. Infer only what it commits the author to.
Reasoning Beyond the Text
AAMC skill 3 · 40% of questions
AAMC's two sub-skills
· Applying or extrapolating ideas from the passage
to new contexts
· Assessing the impact of incorporating new factors,
information, or conditions on ideas from the passage
"The author would most likely respond…" · "Most analogous
to…" · "…if true, would most strengthen/weaken"
Use the passage as a lens on new information.
Errors cascade upward: misread the thesis and you lose the reasoning questions too.
The passage decides the answer — never what you already know.
